examples.title: Storefront — shared model with views
examples.readerQuestion: How do context, container, and component pictures derive from one model?
examples.whenAppropriate: Draft `kdiagram 2` model with embedded views; render with `--view Context`, `--view containers`, or `--view components`.
examples.layoutPolicy: Context: TD stack with company + platform summary node; containers: LR compound boundary; components: LR web | API internals | neighbors
assumptions: One semantic model backs all three views
Context uses an explicit platform node; containers open the commerce boundary; components open apiComponents and exclude the api container shell

examples.title: Order fulfillment — from checkout to warehouse
examples.readerQuestion: What happens after a customer places an order?
examples.whenAppropriate: Container-level architecture with team ownership and sync vs event edges.
examples.layoutPolicy: LR Checkout|Events|Consumers; compact; orthogonal; groupAccent false; named animations
assumptions: Transactional outbox before topic publish
Retry timing omitted; DLQ destination shown

examples.title: Order service — ports and adapters
examples.readerQuestion: How do inbound and outbound adapters surround the order application core?
examples.whenAppropriate: Hexagonal / ports-and-adapters overview for one service.
examples.layoutPolicy: Outer hex row (driving|service surround|driven); nested Application hex + Domain; spacious; groupAccent true
assumptions: CreateOrderCommand is the inbound port; adapters map into it
OrderRepositoryPort is owned by the core; Postgres and in-memory implement it
Inventory and notifications are out of scope for this hexagon

examples.title: Orders API contract
examples.readerQuestion: Who provides the Orders API, and who requires it?
examples.whenAppropriate: A provided/required contract between two components. Use order-hexagon for ports inside one service.
examples.layoutPolicy: LR component | socket | ball | component; compact; orthogonal; groupAccent false
assumptions: The socket opens east
The assembly is ..> from the required interface to the provided interface

examples.title: Order domain — event storm
examples.readerQuestion: What happens in the domain from browse through payment to fulfillment?
examples.whenAppropriate: DDD event-storming discovery timeline. Prefer order-placed-events for runtime fan-out.
examples.layoutPolicy: LR row of Browse|Checkout|Fulfill phase groups; compact; orthogonal; kind subtitles on
assumptions: Kinds carry sticky meaning; no second color system
Phase groups are facilitation columns, not bounded contexts

examples.title: Commerce bounded contexts
examples.readerQuestion: How do catalog, ordering, payments, and fulfillment relate?
examples.whenAppropriate: DDD context map. Distinct from C4 system context in storefront-model.
examples.layoutPolicy: LR compound boundaries; spacious; group accents; orthogonal; checkout integration animation
assumptions: Five contexts teach the map; marketing and tax omitted
Plain-language relationship labels

examples.title: Order aggregate
examples.readerQuestion: What sits inside the Order aggregate?
examples.whenAppropriate: DDD aggregate design. Distinct from order-hexagon ports/adapters.
examples.layoutPolicy: LR command → aggregate boundary → event; compact; orthogonal; kind subtitles on
assumptions: Muted component stands in for a value object
One aggregate is the useful zoom

examples.title: OrderPlaced — event consumers
examples.readerQuestion: Who consumes OrderPlaced and where do exhausted deliveries go?
examples.whenAppropriate: Focused event-driven fan-out after publish.
examples.layoutPolicy: LR Publish|Backbone|Consumers; compact; => for events; groupAccent false
assumptions: Publisher shown as outbox relay plus topic only

examples.title: Order fulfillment — interaction
examples.readerQuestion: In what order do checkout, publish, and consumers interact?
examples.whenAppropriate: Sequence / interaction timing for the fulfillment path.
examples.layoutPolicy: sequence with autonumber, parallel consumers, named animations
assumptions: No Temporal or other orchestrator product

examples.title: Checkout payment — complete sequence
examples.readerQuestion: What does a full sequence look like when authorize, decline, and a short-lived shipment share one timeline?
examples.whenAppropriate: Specimen of sequence constructs: replies, fragments, notes, create, and destroy.
examples.layoutPolicy: sequence with autonumber; fragments hug the participants they mention; create drops Shipment onto the timeline; Funds captured and Declined animations
assumptions: Both captured and declined branches are drawn together
Cart id is the idempotency key

examples.title: Charge a cart — sequence
examples.readerQuestion: What does POST /checkout send, and which async event carries the amount?
examples.whenAppropriate: A sequence of endpoint calls and events where a few messages need a short JSON excerpt.
examples.layoutPolicy: sequence with autonumber; payload cards only on the call, the publish, and the auth reply; Charge authorized animation
assumptions: Amounts are minor units
The cart id is the idempotency key
orders.v1 carries AuthorizeRequested

examples.title: Order lifecycle
examples.readerQuestion: Which order statuses are legal and which transitions move between them?
examples.whenAppropriate: First-class state diagram for lifecycle legality.
examples.layoutPolicy: state surface; LR compact; illustrative guards in labels
assumptions: Guards such as [approved] are illustrative
Ship completes fulfillment without modeling warehouse scans

examples.title: Expense approval
examples.readerQuestion: Who owns each step from submit through policy checks to approval?
examples.whenAppropriate: True swimlane workflow — horizontal responsibility bands with a shared LR timeline.
examples.layoutPolicy: Top-level swimlane groups; inferred groupLayout swimlane + LR; compact; orthogonal; named animations
assumptions: Policy validation is automated
Correction and reject return to the employee

examples.title: Customer refund request
examples.readerQuestion: How does a refund request move through eligibility, inspection, approval, and payout?
examples.whenAppropriate: Business workflow with decisions and owner columns. Prefer expense-approval for true swimlanes.
examples.layoutPolicy: LR compound Support | Finance columns; orthogonal; compact; groupAccent false; Denied animation
assumptions: Support and Finance are owner columns, not TD swimlanes
Policy thresholds are illustrative

examples.title: Checkout schema
examples.readerQuestion: Which tables own checkout data, and how do keys and cardinality relate them?
examples.whenAppropriate: ERD / persistence model for checkout entities.
examples.layoutPolicy: LR compound Identity|Catalog|Orders; compact; orthogonal FK crow’s-feet; groupAccent false
assumptions: PostgreSQL-ish UUID keys and varchar/numeric/char types
One captured payment per order in this slice
Outbox table omitted from this ERD

examples.title: Employee schedules
examples.readerQuestion: Which schedule reads stay in one CouchDB partition, and which rule cannot be atomic?
examples.whenAppropriate: Document model for access paths, partition keys, and single-document invariants.
examples.layoutPolicy: LR access paths then schedules and HR databases; compact compound groups; orthogonal routes
assumptions: CouchDB 3 partitioned databases and Mango indexes
Team-day coverage uses a global index

examples.title: Order fulfillment — review slide
examples.readerQuestion: Same fulfillment story with review chrome and named animations.
examples.whenAppropriate: Presentation / design-review export of a correct architecture graph.
examples.layoutPolicy: Same topology as order-fulfillment; light theme; metro; groupAccent false
assumptions: Topology matches order-fulfillment

examples.title: Language atlas — kinds and edges
examples.readerQuestion: What kinds, content knobs, and edge operators does the language expose?
examples.whenAppropriate: Language catalog — not a system map.
examples.layoutPolicy: TD compact grid of packed catalogs; groupAccent false

examples.title: Geometry kinds
examples.readerQuestion: What geometry kinds and aliases are available?
examples.whenAppropriate: Shape catalog — not a system map.
examples.layoutPolicy: LR 2-column packed shape catalog; groupAccent false

examples.title: Architecture icons
examples.readerQuestion: How do Lucide, logos, and simple-icons appear on architecture nodes?
examples.whenAppropriate: Icon catalog — not a system map.
examples.layoutPolicy: TD 2-column icon packs; no fake topology edges; groupAccent false
